point_reach_env.What is the difference between terminate: Contrast an MDP terminal state (success or failure) with an external cut-off. Name the wrapper that produces the time-limit flag and the comparison it uses on the step counter.
point_reach_env.Why should reset be seeded once and then: Think about what reproducibility means across a run of episodes versus within one. Cover what re-seeding every reset with the same seed does to the variety of starts, and what one seed buys for debugging.
point_reach_env.Why can one step set both terminated and: Separate the two decisions: one depends on the task state, the other only on a counter. Then cover which flag decides whether the value target adds a discounted next-state value.
point_reach_env.Why should a reset to a stored initial s: Think about a replay of a fixed benchmark start placed between ordinary episodes. Cover what happens to every later episode's start if that reset quietly consumes random draws.
point_reach_env.Why must step return new observation ten: Think about rollout buffers that keep every observation. Cover what aliasing one internal tensor does to stored transitions, and to the environment when a caller edits an observation.
point_reach_env.Raising on a step after the episode ends: Weigh loud failure against throughput. Cover how a silent reset can mix the reset observation into the last transition, and what a vector env must do instead to keep workers busy.
point_reach_env.Sparse success reward versus a shaped de: Weigh exploration difficulty against a proxy objective. Cover how a shaped distance term speeds early learning, what behavior it can reward that success alone would not, and how success is still measured.

vla_action_adapter.Why can a VLA's raw output not be sent s: Walk the raw output space: normalized, padded to a shared model width, possibly delta, gripper in a dataset convention. Map each adapter step to which of those it undoes and what goes wrong if it is skipped.
vla_action_adapter.What does a delta mask such as make_bool: Expand the positive and negative counts into a per-dim boolean list. Cover which dims get the state added, why joints suit deltas, and why an open/close gripper command is naturally absolute.
vla_action_adapter.In a chunk of H delta actions, is each s: Compare adding one state to all H steps against a running sum over steps. Cover which reference state openpi uses and what the unsqueeze at dim -2 does for batched chunks.
vla_action_adapter.What does np.sign return for a gripper v: Evaluate both orders on exactly 0.5 and on values in (0, 0.5). Cover sign(0) = 0, what a zero gripper command means to the env, and why the raw [0, 1] value carries no sign information.
vla_action_adapter.Does it matter whether the gripper is fl: Use the odd symmetry of sign. Cover sign(-g) versus -sign(g), including g = 0, and contrast it with a step that would not commute, such as a threshold that maps 0 to +1.
vla_action_adapter.Binarized versus continuous gripper comm: Weigh a smaller effective action space against grasp precision. Cover how a binary gripper affects sampling and exploration, and when partial closing or force control needs continuous values.
vla_action_adapter.Quantile (q01/q99) versus z-score normal: Compare how one outlier moves the mean/std versus the 1st/99th percentiles, and what each openpi inverse does to padded dims (pass-through versus padding stats of mean 0, std 1). Note which model types use which.

chunk_step_executor.Why does a VLA RL rollout need a per-act: Episodes end at arbitrary slots, not chunk boundaries. Cover what the batched simulator returns after an end, and which loss terms (log-probs, advantages) the mask must zero.
chunk_step_executor.Why must the action that ends an episode: Think about where a sparse success reward arrives. Cover what happens to the learning signal if the ending slot is masked out, and how the count relates to the first done index.
chunk_step_executor.A batched GPU simulator cannot pause one: Contrast stepping every env each call with per-env control. Cover the active vector, writing only active rows, and copying results the simulator may overwrite.
chunk_step_executor.In auto-reset mode RLinf folds terminati: Look at flags reported after an env's end, for example a truncation followed by a later success. Cover which fold reports both and why the value target cares.
chunk_step_executor.Which observation should a value functio: Name the true last state of the episode. Cover what the env rows hold after the end, and why truncation bootstraps while termination does not.
chunk_step_executor.Auto-resetting envs inside a chunk versu: Weigh idle simulator steps against bookkeeping. Cover splitting one chunk across two episodes, where the reset observation goes, and how masks and advantages change.
chunk_step_executor.Larger chunks mean fewer policy calls. W: Consider the slowest env in the batch and open-loop execution. Cover wasted steps after early ends, coarser chunk-level rewards and reaction latency.

vector_autoreset.Why does a vectorized environment reset: Think about lock-step batching: episodes end at different times. Cover what idles if the caller must wait, and why a training loop wants a full batch of N envs on every step.
vector_autoreset.For an env whose episode just ended, wha: Compare the call that ends the episode and the call after it. Cover which observation each returns, the reward and flags on the reset, and where SameStep puts the true last observation and info.
vector_autoreset.In NextStep mode, which rows of a rollou: Look at the call after a done. Cover which flags you carry over from the previous call, why that row has no executed action, and where the mask enters the loss and GAE.
vector_autoreset.In SameStep mode, why must a PPO learner: Truncation needs the value of the true last state. Cover what the returned observation is for a reset env, where final_obs lives, and which wrong value the bootstrap would use otherwise.
vector_autoreset.Why does an autoreset call env.reset() w: Think about episode diversity and each env's own RNG. Cover what the seed given to the vector reset is for, and what reusing it on every autoreset would do to the episodes you collect.
vector_autoreset.NextStep versus SameStep for a GPU-batch: Weigh the non-transition rows NextStep produces against SameStep's extra info plumbing. Cover simulator cost per call, buffer masking, and the typical bug each mode invites.
vector_autoreset.Batching info as per-key arrays with mas: Contrast per-key arrays with masks against a list of dicts. Cover vectorized indexing such as final_obs[done_mask], keys some envs lack, nested dicts, and Python-level loops.

episode_metrics_tracker.What is the difference between success_o: Contrast ever reaching the goal with being in the goal state at the last step. Cover a robot that succeeds then knocks the object away, and why the two coincide when a success terminates the episode.
episode_metrics_tracker.Why does a vectorized robot environment: Think about thousands of envs stepping in one batch but finishing at different steps under partial resets. Cover what a single shared total would mix together and which buffers each env needs.
episode_metrics_tracker.With same-step autoreset, why must the e: Follow the order inside one step: record, snapshot, reset the finished envs. Cover what in-place zeroing does to a tensor the caller still holds, and where ManiSkill puts the finished episode's numbers.
episode_metrics_tracker.What changes in the metrics when ignore_: Cover what ends an episode once terminations are ignored (only truncation), what the returned terminations become, and why success_at_end only carries extra information when the episode runs to the time limit.
episode_metrics_tracker.How do Gymnasium's NEXT_STEP and SAME_ST: Compare when the reset happens relative to the done step in each mode. Cover which step's reward and length belong to which episode, and when the running statistics must be zeroed in each case.
episode_metrics_tracker.Partial resets versus running every envi: Weigh simulator throughput and fresh episodes against a fixed horizon for every env. Cover which mode lets you report success_at_end, and how ManiSkill's PPO baseline splits training and evaluation between the two.
episode_metrics_tracker.Averaging finished-episode metrics per s: Think about which episodes finish more often in a fixed number of steps. Cover what averaging the done-step snapshot does to short versus long episodes, and how a per-episode or fixed-episode-count evaluation fixes it.

truncation_bootstrap_gae.What is the difference between terminate: Use Gymnasium's definitions: a terminal state of the MDP versus a condition outside it such as a time limit. Say what V of each next state is, and name partial-episode bootstrapping.
truncation_bootstrap_gae.Why does an auto-resetting vector enviro: Say what observation the env returns on the step an episode ends, where the true last one goes (final_obs), and which state values[t + 1] then describes.
truncation_bootstrap_gae.Walk through the bootstrap value and the: Give boot and cont for each of the three cases, say which flag wins when both are set, and explain why the next row's value is never used at a boundary.
truncation_bootstrap_gae.Why must the GAE trace still be cut at a: Separate the two terms: the bootstrap carries the truncated episode's future, while A[t + 1] belongs to the next episode in the buffer. Say what leaks if the trace is not cut.
truncation_bootstrap_gae.How do you turn per-step rewards inside: Cover the valid mask after an episode ends mid-chunk, the undiscounted sum, folded flags, and that gamma now applies per chunk, so the effective horizon changes. Mention RLinf's chunk_level reward type.
truncation_bootstrap_gae.When is bootstrapping through a time lim: Distinguish tasks whose time limit is part of the objective from limits used only to reset more often. Name the time-aware alternative from Pardo et al. and what it adds to the observation.
truncation_bootstrap_gae.Step-level versus chunk-level advantages: Weigh matching credit to policy decisions and fewer recursion steps against losing within-chunk timing and discounting. Mention how the log-prob is defined per chunk and how gamma must be retuned.

init_state_group_advantage.Why should GRPO groups for a robot polic: Think about what the group mean is supposed to be a baseline for. Cover how object layout changes difficulty under one instruction, and what a mixed-layout baseline ends up rewarding.
init_state_group_advantage.Why do all-success and all-failure group: Write out the numerator of each estimator when every reward in the group is equal. Cover what that means for the gradient and what the rollouts still cost.
init_state_group_advantage.An episode ends after the third action o: Separate generated from executed. Cover what the env worker does on done, what the tokens of the unexecuted actions influenced, and the mask formula in env steps times tokens per action.
init_state_group_advantage.How does the sample standard deviation c: Give the ratio between the two in terms of the group size and when it matters. Then cover the singleton rule (mean 0, std 1) and what advantage it gives a successful lone rollout.
init_state_group_advantage.Why must dropped groups also be removed: Think about the loss reduction, not the numerator. Cover how a token-mean denominator changes when zero-advantage tokens stay in the mask, and which batches that affects most.
init_state_group_advantage.Several rollouts from one initial state: Contrast a per-state baseline with coverage of the initial-state distribution. Cover simulator cost per rollout, how often groups turn out uniform, and what RIPT-VLA's mixed-init option trades.
init_state_group_advantage.Spreading one binary episode outcome ove: Weigh credit assignment against stability and cost. Cover episode length, sparse 0/1 rewards, critic training on images, and what RL4VLA reports for PPO versus GRPO.

flow_sde_chain_logprob.Why can't PPO use the likelihood of an a: Contrast a deterministic Euler step (a point mass) with a Gaussian transition. Cover what PPO's ratio needs, why divergence-based likelihoods are inaccurate with few steps, and what the chain log-density decomposes into.
flow_sde_chain_logprob.What does Flow-SDE change in a denoising: Name the two pieces Flow-SDE adds to the Euler update: a diffusion term with schedule sigma, and a score-based drift. Say what the drift is meant to preserve and how the score is written using the velocity.
flow_sde_chain_logprob.Write the Flow-SDE step mean in terms of: Start from the predicted action x - t v and predicted noise x + (1 - t) v, weighted by 1 - t_next and t_next. Show which weight the correction shrinks, and what the mean collapses to without it.
flow_sde_chain_logprob.The schedule sigma = a * sqrt(t / (1 - t: Look at which part of sigma's formula RLinf changes at t = 1, numerator or denominator, and what it substitutes. Then work out 1 - t_1 on a K-step grid and multiply by sqrt(delta).
flow_sde_chain_logprob.pi_RL runs one randomly chosen denoising: Think of the two-layer MDP: the chosen SDE step is the action and the ODE steps are deterministic. Cover what the stored chain and index let you recompute, how many network calls that takes, and why ODE steps add no density.
flow_sde_chain_logprob.Joint chain log-probability over all K s: Compare network calls per sample, how the log-ratio scales with K (and RLinf's averaging over K + 1 terms), and whether every step or only one explores per rollout.
flow_sde_chain_logprob.Token-level, action-level and chunk-leve: Cover what one ratio multiplies (a single dimension, one action, or the whole chunk), how summing log-probs grows the log-ratio, and how that interacts with a fixed clip range and a single chunk-level advantage.
